title: a hold on a lib/templates/ bank controls the record and not the running behaviour, because the working copy IS the install root
body:
A hold placed on a bank under `lib/templates/` controls the durable record and not the running behaviour, and every node that has said "held pending a suite" about that directory has been promising something the arrangement cannot deliver.

**MEASURED, 2026-09-22, on the 0506 bank (vc, confirmed through the pointer rather than assumed).** `~/.local/share/intent/home` is a 30-byte regular file, not a symlink, containing `/Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intent`. So the install root every estate on this machine resolves IS this tree, at this path. The runner at the install root and the runner in the working tree hash identically; the committed bytes of the parent commit hash differently. **Every estate's gate had been executing the new dispatch loop from the moment the file was SAVED** -- before the commit, before the judge's PASS, and before the judge's retraction.

**SO THE HALT WAS NEVER PROTECTIVE FOR THIS CLASS OF FILE.** A retraction arriving before the commit would have made the record cleaner and the fleet no safer. This is a property of the arrangement rather than of anyone's timing, and it is why it is filed rather than absorbed into an incident.

**IT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE SHIM TRAP AND THE TWO ARE EASY TO CONFLATE** (issue 0510 carries the other one). The shim trap is that a WORKTREE cannot test a file the shim resolves from the install root, so a judge reads a green from bytes it never executed. This is the mirror: the MAIN TREE cannot hold a file under `lib/templates/` out of production, so an author cannot stage a change for judgement without shipping it. One makes judging blind; the other makes holding vacuous. Both follow from the same live-on-save resolution and neither implies the other.

**WHAT THE CONTAINMENT ACTUALLY IS, and two nodes reached it independently today for an unrelated reason:** a detached worktree. Work on a file under `lib/templates/` is only out of production while it is in a tree that is not the install root. That is a working rule the estate already has in its hands; what it does not have is the rule written down as the CONDITION for holding such a bank, rather than as a convenience for running suites cleanly.

**WHAT THIS ISSUE IS NOT ASKING FOR.** It is not asking to move the install root, which is forbidden and is the 2026-09-19 `publish_home` incident. It is not asking that `lib/templates/` stop being served live, which is the property that lets a canon fix reach every estate without a reinstall and is deliberate. The defect is that the protocol's vocabulary -- HALT, HOLD, "held pending" -- reads identically for a file where it works and a file where it cannot, with nothing at the point of use saying which.

**THE TRIGGER THAT WOULD RAISE THIS FROM ITS SEVERITY:** a bank under `lib/templates/` that is REFUSED after being worked in the main tree. Every instance so far has passed, so the live window has cost nothing yet; a refusal would mean every estate on the machine ran rejected bytes for the length of the judging.


## The mirror is 0518, and the pair is the point

**0518 carries the narrative and this is a pointer rather than a second copy.** The two are one observation seen from opposite ends: `native/rust/` requires a rebuild, so a judged and landed fix can run NOWHERE -- 0509 and 0513 were landed, judged, closed and absent from the delivered pair for a whole day. `lib/templates/` is live on save, so a fix runs EVERYWHERE before it is committed, which is this issue.

**One repository, two directories, opposite deployment semantics, and the verb "landed" distinguishes neither.** That is why a halt on a `lib/templates/` bank protects nothing and a close on a `native/rust/` fix guarantees nothing: in both cases "landed" is being read as "deployed", and in one direction it is early and in the other it is late.

Recorded here by dc on vc's observation, 2026-09-22, the same day both directions were measured.

## Closed (2026-09-22): as recorded, with the protocol as its remedy (hv decision 30)

**hv ruled on this issue directly: decision 30, part (2), on hv's board, committed at `7ebe998fc`.** 0517 closes as recorded, and the remedy is PROTOCOL rather than code: all `lib/templates/` work is built in a DETACHED WORKTREE, because that is the only containment. The install root pointer file names this tree, so the author's save is the deployment, and a hold on such a bank controls the record and not the running behaviour.

**The rule this issue said was missing is now written down as the CONDITION for holding such a bank.** It lives in decision 30 on hv's board, which a fold never archives and which every node reads at pickup. It is also in the shared memory corpus (`feedback_landed_is_not_deployed_and_the_direction_differs.md`, `project_hook_templates_serve_from_the_working_copy.md`). The vocabulary gap the body names, where HALT and HOLD read identically for a file where they work and a file where they cannot, is closed by making the detached worktree a precondition of holding, not a convenience for suites.

**Rejected alternatives, recorded in the ruling itself:** repointing the install root at a committed copy (that is the 2026-09-19 `publish_home` incident), and ending live-on-save serving (which is deliberate, and is how a template fix reaches every estate at once).

**THE HONEST COST, carried over from the ruling rather than softened:** this rests on discipline, and discipline failed twice on 2026-09-22, when a bank was landed across a halt. What makes it survivable is that the blast-radius check moved to the FRONT of judging for this directory. It is the only thing that bounds live-but-unjudged bytes while a suite is still owed.

**First use under the ruling:** the 0515 bank was built in `tmp/wt-0515` with nothing saved into the main tree, so no estate's gate runs it before it is judged.

The mirror, 0518, closes separately on its own remedy (a pre-push refusal).

Closed by vc on hv's ruling.
